venue.name: Nature House at Goldstream Provincial Park
venue.description: The Goldstream Nature House sits in Goldstream Provincial Park, about 16 km northwest of Victoria, and is run by Discover Parks, a project of the BC Parks Foundation. Inside are displays about the park's forests, rivers and wildlife, hands-on activities and a gift shop. In summer, Discover Parks Ambassadors run free drop-in nature programs in the park, and in autumn the building becomes the centre of salmon education during the chum salmon run. BC Parks asks school groups and other groups to contact the Nature House directly by email.

facility_notes.washrooms: Please have your group use the washrooms at the day-use picnic shelter before heading down to the Nature House. The washrooms at the Nature House have a very limited number of stalls.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: There are accessible washrooms in close proximity to the picnic shelters. The only trail accessible to wheelchairs is the trail from the picnic shelters to the Nature House (the Visitor Centre Trail) and is approximately 750m. The Nature House is also accessible by ramp.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Free day-use parking is available. The parking lot near the picnic shelters has accessible parking stalls.

restrictions: Pets must be on a leash at all times and are not allowed in beach areas or park buildings.
Fishing is not allowed in Goldstream Provincial Park.
There is no pedestrian access between the east and west sides of Goldstream Provincial Park, bisected by the Trans-Canada Highway.
venue.hours_notes: Open 7 days a week, 9:30am to 3:30pm. Closed on September 23 for fall staff training.
venue.seasonal_notes: Due to structural damage impacting the power supply to the nature house, they are currently operating at a limited capacity. The front desk and retail store remain open and the exhibit space remains temporarily closed. That notice was still on their page in September 2026. In autumn the salmon run is the focus, with the best viewing late October through November.
venue.price_year_or_season: The one school program price we could read, $150 for a program slot, sits on their Goldstream Spring School Programs page, and that page says the activity ended on May 15, 2026.

programs.name: School and group programs
programs.description: BC Parks directs school groups and other groups to contact the Goldstream Nature House by email to arrange a visit or a program. Neither the BC Parks park page nor the Discover Parks Nature House page publishes what those programs cover, what they cost, how long they run or what ages they suit.
programs.our_note: Everything about a group booking here goes through one email address, so allow time for a reply before you fix a date. Ask whether the exhibit space has reopened, because it was shut for repairs when we checked.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing about washrooms, lunch space or where a bus can park is published for the Nature House, and there is no street address on their pages either. An email is the only way to settle the logistics.
programs.evidence: For school groups and special group programs, please contact the Goldstream Nature House at goldstreamnaturehouse@bcparksfoundation.ca.

programs.name: Guided school program at the Nature House
programs.description: A 90 minute guided program run by the Discover Parks Ambassadors, meeting at the Goldstream Nature House. The version we could read is the spring one, and it offers three choices: Bird Detectives for K to 3, Feathers, Facts and Field Science for grades 4 to 7, and Field Science in Action for grades 8 to 12. The fee is $150 per program slot, and one booking covers one adult with one class of 25 students, so two classes means two bookings. Teachers reserve a date and time through the Book Now button on the page and then complete a separate booking form, and the confirmation only comes once both are done. The page says the activity ended on May 15, 2026, so the dates on it have passed.
programs.what_children_do: Meet at the Nature House, then head out into the park with an Ambassador to look for birds, watch how they behave and count what they see, with story time for the youngest groups and note taking for the older ones.
programs.our_note: The $150 buys one 90 minute slot for a class of 25, not a price per child, and you book a second slot for a second class. Teachers and chaperones have to stay with the group the whole time. Ask what is running the term you want, because the page we could read covers a spring season that has already finished.
programs.practical_summary: Send everyone to the washrooms at the day use picnic shelter first, because the Nature House has very few stalls. It is a 750m walk down from the day use area, about ten minutes, and that path is the one route a wheelchair can take.
programs.payment_timing: Booked and paid through the Book Now button on the activity page. A separate booking form must also be completed, and the confirmation email is sent only after both are done.
programs.cancellation_note: To be eligible for a refund, participants must notify us of their cancellation at least 14 days prior to the scheduled program date. Cancellations 14 days or more before the program qualify for a full refund, 7 to 13 days before for a 50% refund, and less than 7 days before are non-refundable but may qualify for rescheduling within six months.
programs.evidence: BC Parks Foundation has implemented a program fee of $150 per program slot

programs.name: Visit to the Nature House
programs.description: A drop-in visit to the Nature House building in the park. Discover Parks lists it as a self-guided activity and describes displays about the park's forests, rivers and wildlife, hands-on activities, and a gift shop whose takings support the education programs. When we checked, the exhibit space was closed because of structural damage and only the front desk and retail store were open. No admission price is published.
programs.what_children_do: Go into the Nature House and look at the displays about the park's forests, river and wildlife, and try the hands-on activities set out inside.
programs.our_note: Check before you set out. When we looked, the exhibit space was shut for repairs and only the front desk and shop were open, which is a thin visit for a group that has travelled out from town.
programs.practical_summary: The building is indoors and open seven days a week through the summer season, but their pages say nothing about washrooms, lunch space or bus parking, and no admission price is given.
programs.evidence: Inside, you'll find engaging displays, hands-on activities, and opportunities to connect with the plants, animals, and ecosystems

programs.name: Free drop-in programs with Discover Parks Ambassadors
programs.description: Discover Parks Ambassadors run free nature education programs at Goldstream Park through the summer, including guided nature walks, evening programs and Jerry's Rangers. Discover Parks says they are in 24 parks from June to August. The per park schedule sits on a page that did not load for us, so the dates and start times are not recorded here.
programs.what_children_do: Join a guided nature walk in the park with an Ambassador, or take part in one of the drop-in activities they set up.
programs.our_note: These are drop-in rather than booked, so they are not something to build a trip around without checking first. Email or phone the Nature House to find out what is running the week you want to come.
programs.practical_summary: Free, outdoors and no booking needed. Washrooms, lunch space and bus parking are not stated on their pages, so ask when you get in touch.
programs.evidence: Ambassadors will be offering free nature education programs such as guided nature walks, evening programs, and Jerry's Rangers in 24 parks across the province.

gaps: no address published, cannot geocode. Neither the Discover Parks Nature House page nor the BC Parks park page gives a street address or coordinates for the Nature House, so the record has no map pin. Ask for the exact meeting point when you email.
price for the school and group programs is not published anywhere on the operator's pages.
youngest age welcomed is not stated, and nothing says whether daycare and preschool groups are taken.
capacity for a group booking is not stated.
lead time for a group booking is not stated.
washrooms, indoor lunch space, rain backup and bus parking are not stated for the Nature House.
